spots.name: Paulista Avenue
spots.summary: Paulista Avenue is one of the most important avenues in São Paulo, Brazil. It stretches 2.8 kilometres (1.7 mi) and runs northwest to southeast.

spots.name: São Paulo Museum of Art
spots.summary: The São Paulo Museum of Art is an art museum in São Paulo, Brazil. It is well known for the architectural significance of its headquarters, a 1968 concrete and glass structure designed by Lina Bo Bardi.

names.nl: Museu de Arte de São Paulo
names.de: Museu de Arte de São Paulo
names.es: Museo de Arte de São Paulo

spots.name: Ibirapuera Park
spots.summary: Ibirapuera Park is an urban park in São Paulo. It comprises 158 hectares between Av. República do Líbano, Av. Pedro Alvares Cabral, and Av. IV Centenário, and is the most visited park in South America, with 14.4 million visits in 2017.

spots.name: São Paulo Cathedral
spots.summary: The Metropolitan Cathedral of Our Lady Assumption and Saint Paul, also known as the See Cathedral, is the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of São Paulo, Brazil.

spots.name: Museu do Ipiranga
spots.summary: The Museu Paulista of the University of São Paulo, commonly known as Museu do Ipiranga, is a Brazilian history museum located near the place where Emperor Pedro I is stated to have proclaimed Brazil's independence on the banks of the Ipiranga Brook, located in the Southeast region of the city of São Paulo — then known as the "Caminho do Mar" — or "road to the seashore".

spots.name: Altino Arantes Building
spots.summary: The Altino Arantes Building, also known as the Banespa Building and most popularly by Banespão, is an important Art Deco skyscraper located in São Paulo, Brazil.

names.ja: アルティーノアランチスビル
names.zh: 阿尔蒂诺·阿兰特斯大厦

spots.name: Edifício Copan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Edifício Copan, or just Copan, is one of the most important and emblematic buildings in the city of São Paulo, located at number 200 Avenida Ipiranga, in the city center, and was inaugurated in 1966.

names.ja: コパン・ビルディング

spots.name: Luz Station
spots.summary: Luz Station is a commuter rail and intercity rail station in the Bom Retiro district of São Paulo, Brazil, serving RFFSA, the intercity rail network of Brazil, CPTM Line 10-Turquoise, Line 11-Coral and Line 13-Jade.

spots.name: Pinacoteca de São Paulo
spots.summary: The Pinacoteca de São Paulo is a visual arts museum focused on Brazilian art from the 19th century to the present day, in dialogue with various cultures from around the world.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Pinacoteca do Estado de São Paulo

spots.name: Monument to the Bandeiras
spots.summary: Monument to the Bandeiras is a large-scale granite sculpture by the Italian-Brazilian sculptor Victor Brecheret (1894-1955) at the entrance of Ibirapuera Park in São Paulo, Brazil. It was commissioned by the government of São Paulo in 1921 and completed in 1954.

spots.name: Obelisk of São Paulo
spots.summary: Obelisk of São Paulo or Obelisk of Ibirapuera is an obelisk in Ibirapuera Park in the city of São Paulo, Brazil.

spots.name: Martinelli Building
spots.summary: The Martinelli Building, with 28 floors, is the first skyscraper built in Brazil. Located in São Paulo, it is 105 meters tall.

names.ja: マルティネッリ・ビル

spots.name: Mirante do Vale

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mirante do Vale, also called Palácio W. Zarzur or Palácio Zarzur Kogan in honour of its architects, is a 170 m (558 ft) mixed-use skyscraper located in São Paulo, Brazil, in the area of Downtown São Paulo and Vale do Anhangabaú.

spots.name: Mosteiro de São Bento
spots.summary: Monastery of Saint Benedict is a Catholic temple located in São Paulo, Brazil. Established on 14 July 1598, the current church was built between 1910 and 1914 by the German architect Richard Berndl.

spots.name: Praça da Sé
spots.summary: Praça da Sé is a public space in São Paulo, Brazil. Considered as the city's central point, it is the point from where the distance of all roads passing through São Paulo are counted. The square was the location of many historical events in São Paulo's history, most notably during the Diretas Já movement.

spots.name: Instituto Butantan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Instituto Butantan is a Brazilian biologic research center located in Butantã, in the western part of the city of São Paulo, Brazil. Instituto Butantan is a public institution affiliated with the São Paulo State Secretariat of Health and considered one of the major scientific centers in the world.

spots.name: Edifício Itália

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Edifício Itália is a 165 m (541 ft) tall 46-story skyscraper located in the República district, Central Zone of São Paulo, Brazil. Built from 1956 to 1965, it has a rooftop observation deck, open for tourists.

spots.name: Theatro Municipal
spots.summary: Municipal Theatre of São Paulo is a theatre in São Paulo, Brazil. It is regarded as one of the landmarks of the city, significant both for its architectural value as well as for its historical importance, having been the venue for the Week of Modern Art in 1922, which revolutionised the arts in Brazil.

spots.name: Independence Park
spots.summary: Independence Park is an urban park in the Ipiranga district of São Paulo, Brazil. The park is located at the site where the prince regent of Brazil, the future Emperor Pedro I, proclaimed the country's independence in 1822.

spots.name: Museum of the Portuguese Language

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of the Portuguese Language is an interactive Portuguese language—and Linguistics/Language Development in general—museum in São Paulo, Brazil. It is housed in the Estação da Luz railway station, in the urban district of the same name.

spots.name: Monument to the Independence of Brazil
spots.summary: The Monument to the Independence of Brazil is a granite and bronze monument located within the Independence Park in São Paulo, Brazil. It is also known as the Ipiranga Monument or the Altar of the Fatherland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to the Independence of Brazil

spots.name: Vale do Anhangabaú
spots.summary: Vale do Anhangabaú is a region in the city center of São Paulo, located between the viaducts do Chá and Santa Ifigênia. It is a public space commonly characterized as park, where events have traditionally been organized, such as public demonstrations, political rallies, presentations and popular shows.

spots.name: Viaduto do Chá
spots.summary: Viaduto do Chá is a viaduct of São Paulo, Brazil. It was the first viaduct built in the city, and was instigated by Jules Martin, a French immigrant to the city. The 240-metre (790 ft) span crosses the Vale do Anhangabaú.

spots.name: Cemitério da Consolação
spots.summary: The Cemitério da Consolação is a cemetery in São Paulo, Brazil. Located along the north side of the Rua da Consolação in the district of Consolação, it was founded on 15 August 1858, with the name of Cemitério Municipal, being the city's first public graveyard.

spots.name: Octávio Frias de Oliveira Bridge
spots.summary: The Octavio Frias de Oliveira bridge, locally known simply as "Ponte Estaiada", is a cable-stayed bridge over the Pinheiros River in the city of São Paulo, Brazil, opened in May 2008.

spots.summary: The São Paulo Museum of Modern Art,, is located in Ibirapuera Park, São Paulo.

spots.name: Praça da República
spots.summary: Praça da República is a park and public square in the República neighborhood of São Paulo, Brazil. The park covers several city blocks between Rua Pedro Américo, Rua Vinte e Quatro de Maio, Avenida Ipiranga, and Avenida São João in the historic center of the city.

spots.name: Bandeirantes Palace
spots.summary: Palácio dos Bandeirantes is a palace in São Paulo, Brazil. It is the seat of the São Paulo state government and the governor's official residence. The palace, located at the Morumbi district, also houses some secretaries and a wide historical and artistic exhibition open to the public.

spots.name: Igreja de Santo Antônio
spots.summary: The Church of Saint Anthony is a Catholic temple located in Patriarca Square, in the center of the Brazilian city of São Paulo. Established in 1592, the current church was completed between 1899 and 1919.

spots.name: Museum of Sacred Art of São Paulo
spots.summary: The Museum of Sacred Art of São Paulo a museum dedicated to the collection and display of sacred art of Brazil. It is located in the Luz neighborhood of São Paulo in the left wing of the Luz Monastery, a religious institution founded in 1774 by Frei Galvão.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Sacred Art of São Paulo

names.de: Museu de Arte Sacra de São Paulo
names.es: Museo de Arte Sacro de São Paulo

spots.name: Matarazzo Building
spots.summary: Matarazzo Building, also known as Palácio do Anhangabaú, is the city hall of the city of São Paulo, Brazil. It belonged to Banespa until 2004, when it was sold to the city government.

spots.name: Municipal Market of São Paulo
spots.summary: The Municipal Market of São Paulo is a large public market in São Paulo, Brazil. It was designed by the architect Francisco Ramos de Azevedo and inaugurated on January 25, 1933 as a wholesale and retail post specializing in fruits, vegetables, cereals, meats, spices, and other food products.

spots.name: Casa das Rosas
spots.summary: Casa das Rosas — Espaço Haroldo de Campos de Poesia e Literatura, is a museum and cultural center in the Paraíso neighborhood of São Paulo, Brazil.

spots.name: Marco Zero
spots.summary: Marco Zero is a geographic monument in downtown São Paulo. In 1934, the marble milestone was installed in front of the São Paulo Cathedral on the Praça da Sé to symbolize the center of the city. The sculpture is a both a tourist attraction and a central point of reference for street numbers in the city.

names.es: Marco cero de la ciudad de São Paulo

spots.name: Pátio do Colégio
spots.summary: Pátio do Colégio is the name given to the historical Jesuit church and school in the city of São Paulo, Brazil. The name is also used to refer to the square in front of the church. The Pátio do Colégio marks the site where the city was founded in 1554.

spots.name: Rua 25 de Março
spots.summary: Rua 25 de Março or Rua Vinte e Cinco de Março is a popular shopping street in the central zone of São Paulo, Brazil. The district surrounding Rua 25 de Março has long been synonymous in Brazil with large crowds and discount shopping.

spots.name: Temple of Solomon
spots.summary: The Temple of Solomon is a replica of the Temple of Solomon built by the Universal Church of the Kingdom of God (UCKG) in São Paulo.

spots.name: Andraus Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Andraus Building is a building in the República area of downtown São Paulo, Brazil, on the corner of Avenida São João and Pedro Américo Street. It is 115 metres tall and has 32 floors, and its construction ended in 1962.

spots.name: Palácio das Indústrias
spots.summary: The Palácio das Indústrias is a historical building in São Paulo, under the protection of the Council for the Defense of Historical, Archaeological, Artistic and Tourist Heritage (CONDEPHAAT).

spots.name: Patriarca Square
spots.summary: The Patriarca Square is located in the Sé district, in the historic center of the Brazilian city of São Paulo.

spots.name: Edifício Wilton Paes de Almeida
spots.summary: The Wilton Paes de Almeida Building was a high-rise building in Largo do Paissandú, São Paulo, Brazil, that was built during the 1960s to be the headquarters of Almeida de Paes, an importer of Belgian glass, featuring its products.

names.zh: 威尔顿·佩斯·德阿尔梅达大楼

spots.name: Largo de São Francisco
spots.summary: Largo de São Francisco is home to some important landmarks in the history of São Paulo and is considered one of the city's main Baroque architecture complexes. It is also known as the "ground zero" of Brigadeiro Luís Antônio, one of the city's most important avenues.

spots.name: Jardim da Luz
spots.summary: Jardim da Luz is a public park near the Luz station and Avenida Tiradentes in the Bom Retiro district of São Paulo. The headquarters of the Pinacoteca do Estado de São Paulo is located in the southeastern corner of the park.

photo.author: Picture taken by pt:Usuário:Gabrielt4e/Foto tirada por pt:Usuário:Gabrielt4e

spots.name: Latin America Memorial
spots.summary: The Latin America Memorial is a cultural, political and leisure complex, inaugurated on March 18, 1989, in São Paulo, Brazil. The architectural setting, designed by Oscar Niemeyer, is a monument to the cultural, political, social and economic integration of Latin America, spanning an area of 84,482 m2 (909,360 sq ft).

spots.name: Football Museum
spots.summary: The Football Museum is a space in the city of São Paulo, Brazil dedicated to the most different subjects involving the practice, history and curiosities revolving around football in Brazil and in the world.

spots.name: Campos Eliseos Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Campos Elíseos Palace, formerly known as the Elias Chaves' Residence, is located on Rio Branco Avenue in the center of São Paulo. It was designed by German architect Matheus Häusler, with construction initiated in 1890 and completed in 1899.

spots.name: Ramos de Azevedo Square
spots.summary: The Ramos de Azevedo Square is located in the República district, in the center of the Brazilian city of São Paulo, and is famous for being home to the Municipal Theater. It was created in 1911, after the theater's inauguration, under the name Esplanada do Theatro.

spots.name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Black Men

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Black Men is located in Largo do Paiçandu, in the central zone of the Brazilian city of São Paulo.

spots.name: Júlio Prestes
spots.summary: Júlio Prestes is a train station on ViaMobilidade Linhas 8 e 9 Line 8-Diamond, located in the district of Santa Cecília in São Paulo. This historical station was named after former Governor of São Paulo and former President-elect of Brazil, Júlio Prestes. Currently, the station serves only Line 8-Diamond.

names.ja: ジュリオ・プレステス

spots.name: Palácio da Justiça
spots.summary: The Palace of Justice is the seat of the Court of Justice of the state of São Paulo. It is located in the old center of the city of São Paulo, between the squares Praça da Sé, Praça João Mendes Jr., and Praça Clóvis Bevilácqua, near the São Paulo Cathedral, the Anchieta Palace and the Matarazzo Building.

spots.summary: The Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral of São Paulo, also known as the Orthodox Cathedral of São Paulo, is a cathedral of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch, located at 1515 Vergueiro in Paraíso, Vila Mariana, São Paulo, Brazil.

spots.summary: The Cinemateca Brasileira is the institution responsible for preserving Brazilian audiovisual production. In July 2021, it experienced a major fire.

spots.summary: A creepy-looking church in a small street near Liberdade Sq., it is one of the oldest surviving churches of the city, dating back to 1774, when it was built to be the chapel of the city's first cemetery. It is still the destination of romaria Catholic pilgrimages.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Igreja Nossa Senhora da Consolação is located in the Consolação neighborhood in the Brazilian city of São Paulo. It was founded in 1799 and reformed in 1840. The current building was designed by the German engineer Maximilian Emil Hehl and built between 1909 and 1959 at the location of the original temple.

spots.name: Portuguese Language Museum
spots.summary: A interactive linguistics museum that shows the different accents and dialects of Portuguese in Europe, Africa, Asia and South America, as well as its relation to other tongues and their developments and influence of African, Amerindian, Asian and European languages on Brazilian Portuguese.

spots.name: Anhangabaú Palace

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: São Paulo's city hall is a building from the 1930s in modernist architectural style. The building had been the home of Matarazzo Industries, which used to be the most powerful manufacturing company in Brazil.

spots.name: República Square
spots.summary: There are buildings that bear witness to many different architectural styles: the 1935 Esther building, considered the first with a modern architectural design; the S-shaped Copan building designed by Oscar Niemeyer; and Itália building (see [[#Historical buildings

spots.name: Japan House
spots.summary: A museum about Japanese art and culture, with rotating exhibits, a cafe, and a library of Japanese literature.

spots.name: Parque Tenente Siqueira Campos
spots.summary: Built in 1892, this small park is the most significant green area of the Paulista region. It combines features of an English garden with preserved Atlantic rainforest, plus landscaping by Roberto Burle Marx and sculptures by Clóvis Olga and Victor Brecheret.

spots.name: Buenos Aires Park
spots.summary: One of the few green areas in the Center, it contains bronze statues by France artists, some built into fountains.

spots.name: Itaú Cultural
spots.summary: A large cultural center that hosts performances and exhibitions. Two of the permanent exhibitions include a showcase of art depicting Brazil from the view of its colonists, and a showcase of Brazilian currency throughout the ages.

spots.name: Pavilhão Japonês
spots.summary: Based on the Katsura Imperial Villa in Kyoto, it was built in 1954 to celebrate the Brazil-Japan relationship. Uses materials imported from Japan in its construction, such as wood and rocks.

photo.author: Niels Elgaard Larsen - User: (WT-shared) Elgaard at wts wikivoyage

spots.name: Centro Cultural FIESP
spots.summary: This pyramid-shaped building is home to the Federação das Indústrias do Estado de São Paulo, a powerful union that represents employees from over 150,000 companies, or 42% of the Brazilian GDP. It also hosts cultural expositions and Teatro Popular do SESI, with high quality theatrical performances.

spots.name: Instituto Moreira Salles
spots.summary: A museum that features an arts and media archive, alongside nice views of the avenue from its upper floors.

spots.name: Paróquia São Luís Gonzaga
spots.summary: This church was built in 1932, constructed in Greek-Roman architecture, in high contrast with the modern buildings surrounding it.

spots.name: Escola Estadual Rodrigues Alves
spots.summary: A public school from 1909, still fully active. It contains a neoclassical European style of architecture, in striking yellow.

spots.name: Chi Fu
spots.summary: A Chinese restaurant famous for authentic and tasty Cantonese dishes with cheap and generous portions. Communicating with the staff can be a challenge, as many only speak Chinese, but the food is worth the while. Reservations only for groups. All the tables are large, so if going alone or in a smaller group of 2-4, you may have to share a table with other customers, Chinese-style. Check out the in

spots.name: Nandemoyá
spots.summary: If you are the kind of tourist who doesn't like to feel at all like a tourist, check this "factory-style" restaurant immensely popular among workers in the region, with long lines, self-service catering, and capacity for 400 people. The quality and diversity of food (Japanese, Chinese and Brazilian) will surely impress you. Many people come here to pile on high-quality sashimi at prices much lower

spots.name: Mocotó
spots.summary: While the menu signed by chef Rodrigo Oliveira and the Michelin Bib Gourmand award may make you think of this as a high-end fancy pants establishment, the atmosphere is casual and the dishes are very straightforward Northeastern Brazilian food, mostly focused on the raw quality of the cooking. Try the dadinhos de tapioca (tapioca squares) and the vegan moqueca (stew).

spots.name: Shawarma Aladdin
spots.summary: Europeans might know the dish as döner kebab due to its Turkish diaspora, but São Paulo was more influenced by Syrian and Lebanese immigration, thus meat cuts with vegetables on a flat bread is known as shawarma. This establishment offers cheap, tasty shawarma with a variety of fillings and sides.

spots.name: A Baianeira
spots.summary: Finish your museum visit here, where you can taste a unique mix of food from Bahia and Minas Gerais with international fine dining influence. The baião de dois with beef stew is a popular option, and can be finished by a banana crème brulée. Vegetarian and vegan options are also available.

spots.name: Mercado Municipal da Lapa
spots.summary: If you're looking for something similar to the Mercadão (big market) found in Downtown, but with less tourists and cheaper, this makes for a good choice. Of particular note is the Pastelaria Mercadão (Box 40/42), a shop which serves particularly large pastéis (deep-fried turnovers).

spots.name: Taverna Medieval
spots.summary: Heavily themed fantasy restaurant, with creative dishes (try the onions with pork) and unique "potion" drinks. Also offers activities such as bow shooting. Reservations are always required, with 15+ person groups requiring a reservation at least 20 days in advance.

spots.name: Rong He
spots.summary: Chinese restaurant with a huge menu specializing in noodle dishes. At the right-hand corner of the main room, behind a glass window, the cook displays his ability to shape yakisoba noodles by hand. Seafood yakisoba is a good choice for 2-3 people to share.

spots.name: Pikurrucha's Perdizes
spots.summary: Beautifully decorated cafe, full of pink furniture, flowers and bears. There's a variety of sweets, pastries and drinks if you have a sweet tooth, the rabanada (French toast) with ice cream is especially recommended. Zero-sugar sweets are also available.

spots.name: Balcão
spots.summary: This old-school bar used to be a meeting spot for journalists but is now used as a venue to promote indie books. Extensive cocktail menu served in a single, large table (rather than smaller tables for groups of guests), making for a good social space.

spots.name: Bolinha
spots.summary: Offering four types of feijoada plus various à la carte items including fish, meat dishes, pasta, and pizza. If you've never tried feijoada, this is a good place to have your first experience. A kosher feijoada is available if requested in advance.

spots.name: Frida & Mina
spots.summary: Ice cream parlor that focuses on locally produced flavors and cones. Flavors swap out daily, with vegan options available. Many surprising choices might be available, such as cupuaçu fruit with chocolate, salty caramel and even beer with chocolate.

spots.name: Panetteria ZN
spots.summary: This bakery is famed for its 1kg coxinha, allowing costumers to take on a challenge where it becomes free of charge if you eat it under 10 minutes. Normal-sized coxinhas are also available, and they are some of the very best in the city.

spots.name: Bar Brahma
spots.summary: One of the best places in São Paulo for live music, especially on Thursday and Sunday, when traditional samba plays. This bar was opened in the 1920s and is the most traditional place to hear classics of Brazilian Popular Music (MPB).

spots.name: Bar do Luiz Fernandes
spots.summary: Active since 1970, this establishment became a favorite among locals for its snacks, drinks and easygoing atmosphere. Aside from their self-brewed beer and non-alcoholic drink menu, their bolinho fried snacks are well worth a try.

spots.name: Castelos Bar & Boardgames
spots.summary: A bar with unique gimmicky drinks, snacks, burgers and a large selection of board and card games to play. The games are free, you pay only for food and drinks. Advance reservations are not required but recommended.

spots.name: Skye
spots.summary: As fancy as the hotel it's housed in, this bar makes for a high-end drinking experience, with its bold decor and finely-crafted dishes. Works as a restaurant and serves breakfast earlier in the day as well.

spots.name: Café Piu Piu
spots.summary: The place to go for live music, especially jazz and blues. Has an old world feel with marble bar tops and antique balconies, but it's the perfect place to hear good music.

spots.name: Rei da Batidas
spots.summary: A traditional boteco (Brazil-specific bar style), popular with USP students, has been operating since 1970. Plenty of chairs on the outside to sit and chat.

spots.name: Posto 6
spots.summary: Aside from a long list of drinks and meals, you can also catch sports on its three televisions and listen to live music alongside a feijoada on Sundays.
